title.zh: 卷四十七 志第三十七 百官二
title.raw: 卷四十七 志第三十七 百官二 Volume 47 Treatises 42: Official Posts 2

meta.sourceNote: Body replaced from Wikisource raw text after ChineseNotes scrape due to glyph/encoding artifacts.

sentences.zh: 門下省侍中二人，正二品。

translations.literal: In the Chancellery there were two Vice Grand Councilors, of the upper second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery had two Vice Grand Councilors, ranked at upper second grade.

sentences.zh: 掌出納帝命，相禮儀。

translations.literal: They managed receiving and issuing the emperor's commands and assisted with ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: They handled the reception and transmission of imperial orders and assisted with court ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 凡國家之務，與中書令參總，而顓判省事。

translations.literal: For all affairs of state they consulted and oversaw together with the Grand Secretary, and held sole authority to decide matters of their department.
translations.idiomatic: On all matters of state they deliberated jointly with the Grand Secretary and held exclusive authority to decide affairs within the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 下之通上，其制有六：一曰奏鈔，以支度國用、授六品以下官、斷流以下罪及除免官用之；

translations.literal: The means for subordinates to communicate upward had six forms: first, the memorial slip, used to authorize state expenditures, appoint officials of the sixth rank and below, adjudicate crimes below exile, and order removal or dismissal from office;
translations.idiomatic: Communications from below to the throne took six established forms. The first was the memorial slip (zou chao), used to authorize state expenditures, appoint officials of sixth rank or lower, judge offenses short of exile, and order demotion or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 二曰奏彈；

translations.literal: Second, the impeachment memorial;
translations.idiomatic: second, the impeachment memorial;

sentences.zh: 三曰露布；

translations.literal: Third, the battlefield bulletin;
translations.idiomatic: third, the battlefield bulletin;

sentences.zh: 四曰議；

translations.literal: Fourth, deliberation;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, deliberation;

sentences.zh: 五曰表；

translations.literal: Fifth, the formal petition;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the formal petition (biao);

sentences.zh: 六曰狀。

translations.literal: Sixth, the memorial of fact.
translations.idiomatic: and sixth, the memorial of fact (zhuang).

sentences.zh: 自露布以上乃審；

translations.literal: From battlefield bulletins upward they were examined;
translations.idiomatic: From battlefield bulletins upward, documents required examination by the Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 其餘覆奏，畫制可而授尚書省。

translations.literal: The rest were returned with a countersignature; once approved in the margin they were passed to the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: the remainder were returned with a countersignature, and once marked approved in the margin were forwarded to the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 行幸，則負寶以從，版奏中嚴、外辦；

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled, they carried the imperial seal and followed; they announced the mid-watch curfew from the board and the outer preparations;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, they carried the imperial seal and accompanied him, announcing the mid-watch curfew from the board and the outer preparations;

sentences.zh: 還宮，則請降輅、解嚴。

translations.literal: On return to the palace they requested descent from the carriage and lifting of the curfew.
translations.idiomatic: On return to the palace they requested that the emperor descend from his carriage and that the curfew be lifted.

sentences.zh: 皇帝齋，則請就齋室；

translations.literal: When the emperor observed abstinence, they invited him to the fasting chamber;
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor undertook ritual fasting, they invited him to the fasting chamber;

sentences.zh: 將奠，則奉玉、幣；

translations.literal: When the offering was about to be made, they presented jade and silks;
translations.idiomatic: When the offering was about to be made, they presented the jade and silken offerings;

sentences.zh: 盥，則奉匜、取盤，酌罍水，贊洗；

translations.literal: For washing, they presented the pitcher, took the basin, poured water from the jar, and intoned the washing rite;
translations.idiomatic: For the ritual washing, they presented the pitcher, took up the basin, poured water from the jar, and intoned the washing rite;

sentences.zh: 酌泛齊，受虛爵，進福酒，皆左右其儀。

translations.literal: Pouring the first libation, receiving the empty cup, presenting the blessing wine—all these they directed on either side.
translations.idiomatic: Pouring the first libation, receiving the empty cup, presenting the blessing wine—they directed each of these rites on either side of the emperor.

sentences.zh: 饗宗廟，進瓚而贊酌鬱酒；

translations.literal: At sacrifices in the ancestral temple, they advanced the libation cup and intoned the pouring of the fragrant wine;
translations.idiomatic: At sacrifices in the ancestral temple, they advanced the libation cup and intoned the pouring of the fragrant sacrificial wine;

sentences.zh: 既祼，贊酌醴齊。

translations.literal: After the libation of unmixed wine, they intoned the pouring of the clear wine.
translations.idiomatic: After the libation of unmixed wine, they intoned the pouring of the clear wine.

sentences.zh: 籍田，則奉耒。

translations.literal: At the plowing ceremony they presented the plough.
translations.idiomatic: At the ceremonial plowing of the sacred field, they presented the plough.

sentences.zh: 四夷朝見，則承詔勞問。

translations.literal: When the four barbarians came to court, they received the edict and offered greetings.
translations.idiomatic: When peoples of the four directions came to court, they received the imperial edict and conveyed the emperor's greetings.

sentences.zh: 臨軒命使冊皇后、皇太子，則承詔降宣命。

translations.literal: When the emperor at the hall appointed envoys to invest the empress or crown prince, they received the edict and transmitted the proclamation downward.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor at the hall appointed envoys to invest the empress or crown prince, they received the edict and transmitted the proclamation of appointment.

sentences.zh: 慰問、聘召，則涖封題。

translations.literal: For condolences, inquiries, or summons they personally sealed and inscribed the documents.
translations.idiomatic: For messages of condolence, inquiry, or summons, they personally sealed and inscribed the documents.

sentences.zh: 發驛遣使，則給魚符。

translations.literal: When dispatching couriers by post-station they issued fish tallies.
translations.idiomatic: When dispatching couriers by post relay, they issued fish tallies as credentials.

sentences.zh: 凡官爵廢置、刑政損益，授之史官；

translations.literal: For all abolition or establishment of offices and ranks, and increases or reductions in penal administration, they handed records to the historiographers;
translations.idiomatic: For all abolition or establishment of offices and ranks, and for increases or reductions in penal administration, they handed records to the historiographers;

sentences.zh: 既書，復涖其記注。

translations.literal: After they were written, they again personally supervised the annal entries.
translations.idiomatic: Once written, they again personally supervised the annal entries.

sentences.zh: 職事官六品以下進擬，則審其稱否而進退之。

translations.literal: For nominations of functional officials of the sixth rank and below, they examined fitness and advanced or rejected them.
translations.idiomatic: For nominations of functional officials of sixth rank and below, they examined whether candidates were suitable and advanced or rejected them.

sentences.zh: 武德元年改侍內曰納言，三年曰侍中。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude the title Palace Attendant was changed to Nazayan; in the third year to Shizhong.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 (618) the title Palace Attendant was changed to Nazayan; in Wude 3 (620) it became Shizhong (Vice Grand Councilor).

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改門下省曰東臺，侍中曰左相，武后光宅元年曰納言，垂拱元年改門下省曰鸞臺。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo the Chancellery was renamed the Eastern Terrace and Shizhong to Left Minister; in the first year of Guangzhai under Empress Wu it became Nazayan; in the first year of Chuigong the Chancellery was renamed the Phoenix Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 (662) the Chancellery was renamed the Eastern Terrace and Shizhong became Left Minister; under Empress Wu in Guangzhai 1 (684) the title became Nazayan; in Chuigong 1 (685) the Chancellery was renamed the Phoenix Terrace.

sentences.zh: 開元元年曰黃門省，侍中曰監，天寶元年曰左相。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kaiyuan it was the Yellow Gate Department; Shizhong was Supervisor; in the first year of Tianbao, Left Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 1 (713) it was the Yellow Gate Department and Shizhong was Supervisor; in Tianbao 1 (742) the title again became Left Minister.

sentences.zh: 門下侍郞二人，正三品。

translations.literal: Two Vice Chancellors of the Chancellery, upper third rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery had two Vice Chancellors, ranked at upper third grade.

sentences.zh: 掌貳侍中之職。

translations.literal: They assisted in the duties of the Vice Grand Councilors.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted the Vice Grand Councilors in their duties.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀則從；

translations.literal: On great sacrifices they accompanied;
translations.idiomatic: On great sacrifices they accompanied the emperor;

sentences.zh: 盥則奉巾，旣帨，奠巾；

translations.literal: For washing they presented the towel; once the towel was tied on, they placed the towel;
translations.idiomatic: for ritual washing they presented the towel; once it was tied on, they set out the towel;

sentences.zh: 奉匏爵贊獻。

translations.literal: They presented the gourd cup and intoned the offering.
translations.idiomatic: they presented the gourd cup and intoned the offering.

sentences.zh: 元日、冬至，奏天下祥瑞。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice they reported auspicious omens from throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day and the winter solstice they reported auspicious omens from throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 侍中闕，則涖封符券、給傳驛。

translations.literal: When the Vice Grand Councilor post was vacant, they personally sealed tally documents and issued post relays.
translations.idiomatic: When the post of Vice Grand Councilor was vacant, they personally sealed tally documents and issued post relays.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年改黃門侍郎曰東臺侍郎，武后垂拱元年曰鸞臺侍郎，天寶元年曰門下侍郎，乾元元年曰黃門侍郎，大曆二年復舊。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 Yellow Gate Vice Chancellor became Eastern Terrace Vice Chancellor; in Chuigong 1 under Empress Wu, Phoenix Terrace Vice Chancellor; in Tianbao 1, Chancellery Vice Chancellor; in Qianyuan 1, Yellow Gate Vice Chancellor; in Dali 2 the former titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 (662) the title became Eastern Terrace Vice Chancellor; under Empress Wu in Chuigong 1 (685) it was Phoenix Terrace Vice Chancellor; in Tianbao 1 (742) Chancellery Vice Chancellor; in Qianyuan 1 (758) Yellow Gate Vice Chancellor; in Dali 2 (767) the original title was restored.

sentences.zh: 左散騎常侍二人，正三品下。

translations.literal: Two Left Masters of Regular Attendance, lower upper third rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Left Masters of Regular Attendance, ranked at lower upper third grade.

sentences.zh: 掌規諷過失，侍從顧問。

translations.literal: They managed remonstrance and admonition regarding faults, and attended the emperor as advisers.
translations.idiomatic: They remonstrated regarding faults, attended the emperor, and served as advisers.

sentences.zh: 隋廢散騎常侍。

translations.literal: The Sui abolished the Masters of Regular Attendance.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dynasty had abolished the office of Master of Regular Attendance.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年復置，十七年為職事官。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 1 it was restored; in the seventeenth year it became a functional office.
translations.idiomatic: It was restored in Zhenguan 1 (627) and in the seventeenth year (643) became a substantive functional office.

sentences.zh: 顯慶二年，分左右，隸門下、中書省，皆金蟬、珥貂、左散騎與侍中為左貂，右散騎與中書令為右貂，謂之八貂。

translations.literal: In Xianqing 2 they were divided into left and right, subordinate to the Chancellery and Secretariat; all wore golden cicadas and earrings with sable tails; the left Master of Regular Attendance with the Vice Grand Councilor formed the left sable group, the right with the Grand Secretary the right sable group—called the Eight Sables.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 2 (657) the office was divided into left and right, attached to the Chancellery and Secretariat respectively. All wore golden cicada insignia and sable-tail earrings; the left Master of Regular Attendance with the Vice Grand Councilor formed the left sable group, and the right with the Grand Secretary the right sable group—together called the Eight Sables.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年曰侍極。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 it was called Attendant of the Utmost.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 (662) the title was changed to Attendant of the Utmost.

sentences.zh: 左諫議大夫四人，正四品下。

translations.literal: Four Left Grand Masters of Remonstrance, lower upper fourth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Left Grandees of Remonstrance, ranked at lower upper fourth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌諫諭得失，侍從贊相。

translations.literal: They managed remonstrance and instruction regarding right and wrong, attended the emperor, and assisted in praise.
translations.idiomatic: They remonstrated regarding right and wrong, attended the emperor, and assisted in court proceedings.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱二年，有魚保宗者，上書請置匭以受四方之書，乃鑄銅匭四，塗以方色，列于朝堂：青匭曰「延恩」，在東，告養人勸農之事者投之；

translations.literal: In Chuigong 2 under Empress Wu, one Yu Baozong submitted a memorial requesting chests to receive writings from all directions; four bronze chests were cast, painted in the colors of the four directions, and set out in the court hall: the green chest called 'Extended Grace,' in the east, for reports on supporting the people and encouraging agriculture;
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 2 (686) under Empress Wu, a man named Yu Baozong submitted a memorial requesting complaint boxes to receive writings from all quarters. Four bronze boxes were cast, painted in the colors of the four directions, and placed in the court hall. The green box, called Extended Grace, stood in the east; reports on caring for the people and encouraging agriculture were deposited in it;

sentences.zh: 丹匭曰「招諫」，在南，論時政得失者投之；

translations.literal: the red chest called 'Summoning Remonstrance,' in the south, for discussion of gains and losses in current policy;
translations.idiomatic: the red box, called Summoning Remonstrance, stood in the south; critiques of current policy were deposited in it;

sentences.zh: 白匭曰「申冤」，在西，陳抑屈者投之；

translations.literal: the white chest called 'Pleading Injustice,' in the west, for stating grievances of oppression;
translations.idiomatic: the white box, called Pleading Injustice, stood in the west; accounts of oppression and wrong were deposited in it;

sentences.zh: 黑匭曰「通玄」，在北，告天文、祕謀者投之。

translations.literal: the black chest called 'Communicating the Mysterious,' in the north, for reports on astronomy and secret plots.
translations.idiomatic: and the black box, called Communicating the Mysterious, stood in the north; reports on astronomy and secret plots were deposited in it.

sentences.zh: 以諫議大夫、補闕、拾遺一人充使，知匭事；

translations.literal: One Grand Master of Remonstrance, Omissioner, or Petitioner was appointed commissioner to manage the chests;
translations.idiomatic: One Grand Master of Remonstrance, Omissioner, or Petitioner was appointed commissioner to manage the boxes;

sentences.zh: 御史中丞、侍御史一人，為理匭使。

translations.literal: one Vice Censor-in-Chief or Attending Censor served as commissioner for adjudicating the chests.
translations.idiomatic: and one Vice Censor-in-Chief or Attending Censor served as commissioner for adjudicating submissions from the boxes.

sentences.zh: 其後，同為一匭。

translations.literal: Later they were combined into one chest.
translations.idiomatic: Later the four were combined into a single box.

sentences.zh: 天寶九載，玄宗以「匭」聲近「鬼」，改理匭使為獻納使，至德元年復舊。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Tianbao, because the pronunciation of 'chest' was close to 'ghost,' Xuanzong changed the title to Commissioner for Presenting Petitions; in Zhide 1 the former title was restored.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 9 (750), because the word for complaint box (gui) sounded like the word for ghost (gui), Emperor Xuanzong changed the title to Commissioner for Presenting Petitions; in Zhide 1 (756) the former title was restored.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，命中書門下擇正直清白官一人知匭，以給事中、中書舍人為理匭使。

translations.literal: In Baoying 1 the Secretariat and Chancellery were ordered to select one upright and incorrupt official to manage the chests; the Drafting Attendant and Secretariat Drafter served as commissioners for adjudicating the chests.
translations.idiomatic: In Baoying 1 (762) the Secretariat and Chancellery were ordered to select one upright and incorrupt official to manage the boxes; Drafting Attendants and Secretariat Drafters served as commissioners for adjudicating submissions.

sentences.zh: 建中二年，以御史中丞為理匭使，諫議大夫一人為知匭使；

translations.literal: In Jianzhong 2 the Vice Censor-in-Chief became commissioner for adjudicating the chests, and one Grand Master of Remonstrance commissioner for managing the chests;
translations.idiomatic: In Jianzhong 2 (781) the Vice Censor-in-Chief became commissioner for adjudicating submissions, and one Grand Master of Remonstrance commissioner for managing the boxes;

sentences.zh: 投匭者，使先驗副本。

translations.literal: those who submitted to the chests had their copies verified first by the commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: and those who submitted petitions had their copies verified first by the commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開成三年，知匭使李中敏以為非所以廣聰明而慮幽枉也，乃奏罷驗副封。

translations.literal: In Kaicheng 3 the commissioner Li Zhongmin held that this was not the way to broaden intelligence and consider hidden wrongs, and memorialized to abolish verification of duplicate seals.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaicheng 3 (838) Commissioner Li Zhongmin argued that this practice did not broaden the ruler's understanding or address hidden wrongs, and memorialized to abolish verification of duplicate seals.

sentences.zh: 武德元年置諫議大夫，龍朔二年曰正諫大夫，貞元四年分左右。

translations.literal: The Grand Master of Remonstrance was established in Wude 1; in Longshuo 2 it was called Rectifying Remonstrance Grand Master; in Zhenyuan 4 it was divided into left and right.
translations.idiomatic: The office of Grand Master of Remonstrance was established in Wude 1 (618); in Longshuo 2 (662) it was renamed Rectifying Remonstrance Grand Master; in Zhenyuan 4 (788) it was divided into left and right.

sentences.zh: 給事中四人，正五品上。

translations.literal: Four Drafting Attendants, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Drafting Attendants, ranked at upper fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌侍左右，分判省事，察弘文館繕寫讎校之課。

translations.literal: They attended on the left and right, divided adjudication of departmental affairs, and inspected the duties of copying and collation at the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: They attended at the emperor's side, shared adjudication of departmental affairs, and inspected copying and collation duties at the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 凡百司奏抄，侍中既審，則駮正違失。

translations.literal: For all memorial slips from the hundred offices, once the Vice Grand Councilor had examined them, they corrected errors.
translations.idiomatic: For all memorial slips from the hundred offices, once the Vice Grand Councilor had examined them, the Drafting Attendants corrected errors.

sentences.zh: 詔敕不便者，塗竄而奏還，謂之「塗歸」。

translations.literal: When edicts and orders were inconvenient, they altered them and returned them with a memorial—called 'return by alteration.'
translations.idiomatic: When edicts and orders were unsuitable, they altered the text and returned them with a memorial—a practice called 'return by alteration' (tu gui).

sentences.zh: 季終，奏駮正之目。

translations.literal: At the end of each season they reported the list of corrections.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of each season they reported the list of corrections they had made.

sentences.zh: 凡大事，覆奏；

translations.literal: For all major matters they countersigned and memorialized;
translations.idiomatic: On all major matters they countersigned and memorialized;

sentences.zh: 小事，署而頒之。

translations.literal: for minor matters they signed and promulgated them.
translations.idiomatic: on minor matters they signed and promulgated them.

sentences.zh: 三司詳決失中，則裁其輕重。

translations.literal: When the three offices' detailed judgments were in error, they determined the severity.
translations.idiomatic: When the three judicial offices' detailed judgments were in error, they determined the appropriate severity.

sentences.zh: 發驛遣使，則與侍郎審其事宜。

translations.literal: When dispatching couriers by post-station they examined the matter together with the Vice Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: When dispatching couriers by post relay, they examined the matter together with the Vice Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 六品以下奏擬，則校功狀殿最、行藝，非其人，則白侍中而更焉。

translations.literal: For nominations of the sixth rank and below submitted as memorials, they checked merit records for achievement ratings and conduct; if the person was unsuitable, they informed the Vice Grand Councilor and had the nomination changed.
translations.idiomatic: For nominations of sixth rank and below, they checked merit records for achievement ratings and conduct; if the candidate was unsuitable, they informed the Vice Grand Councilor and had the nomination changed.

sentences.zh: 與御史、中書舍人聽天下冤滯而申理之。

translations.literal: Together with censors and Secretariat Drafters they heard grievances and wrongs throughout the realm and addressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Together with censors and Secretariat Drafters they heard grievances and wrongs throughout the realm and sought to redress them.

sentences.zh: 門下省有錄事四人，從七品上；

translations.literal: The Chancellery had four Recording Clerks, upper seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: The Chancellery had four Recording Clerks, ranked at upper seventh grade;

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: four Section Chiefs, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and four Section Chiefs, ranked at lower eighth grade.

sentences.zh: 有令史二十二人，書令史四十三人，甲庫令史十三人，能書一人，傳制二人，亭長六人，掌固十四人，脩補制敕匠五人，裝潢一人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-two Clerks, forty-three Clerks for Documents, thirteen Clerks for the A Storehouse, one skilled calligrapher, two Transmission Clerks, six Station Chiefs, fourteen Custodians, five Craftsmen for Repairing and Supplementing Edicts, and one Binder.
translations.idiomatic: It also had twenty-two Clerks, forty-three Document Clerks, thirteen Storehouse Clerks, one skilled calligrapher, two Transmission Clerks, six Station Chiefs, fourteen Custodians, five craftsmen for repairing and supplementing edicts, and one binder.

sentences.zh: 起居郎領令史三人，贊者六人。

translations.literal: The Diarist supervised three Clerks and six Announcers.
translations.idiomatic: The Diarist supervised three Clerks and six Announcers.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，改給事郎曰給事中。

translations.literal: In Wude 3 the Drafting Attendant was changed to Drafting Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 (620) the title Drafting Attendant was changed to Drafting Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 左補闕六人，從七品上；

translations.literal: Six Left Omissioners, upper seventh rank;
translations.idiomatic: There were six Left Omissioners, ranked at upper seventh grade;

sentences.zh: 左拾遺六人，從八品上。

translations.literal: six Left Petitioners, upper eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: and six Left Petitioners, ranked at upper eighth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌供奉諷諫，大事廷議，小則上封事。

translations.literal: They managed attendance, remonstrance, and admonition; on major matters they debated in court; on minor matters they submitted sealed memorials.
translations.idiomatic: They attended court, remonstrated and admonished; on major matters they debated in open court, on minor matters they submitted sealed memorials.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱元年，置補闕、拾遺，左右各二員。

translations.literal: In Chuigong 1 under Empress Wu, Omissioners and Petitioners were established, two on the left and two on the right.
translations.idiomatic: In Chuigong 1 (685) under Empress Wu, the offices of Omissioner and Petitioner were established, with two on the left and two on the right.

sentences.zh: 起居郎二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Two Diarists, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Diarists, ranked at upper sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌錄天子起居法度。

translations.literal: They managed recording the emperor's daily conduct and protocol.
translations.idiomatic: They recorded the emperor's daily conduct and protocol.

sentences.zh: 天子御正殿，則郎居左，舍人居右。

translations.literal: When the emperor attended the main hall, the Diarist stood on the left and the Diarist-Recorder on the right.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor attended the main hall, the Diarist stood on the left and the Diarist-Recorder on the right.

sentences.zh: 有命，俯陛以聽，退而書之，季終以授史官。

translations.literal: When there was a command they bowed at the steps to listen, withdrew and wrote it down, and at the end of the season handed it to the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor gave orders they bowed at the steps to listen, withdrew to write them down, and at the end of each season handed the records to the historiographers.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，以給事中、諫議大夫兼知起居注，或知起居事。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan, Drafting Attendants and Grand Masters of Remonstrance concurrently managed the Daily Records, or managed diarist affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenguan era, Drafting Attendants and Grandees of Remonstrance were concurrently assigned to manage the Daily Records or diarist affairs.

sentences.zh: 每仗下，議政事，起居郎一人執筆記錄于前，史官隨之。

translations.literal: After each court session, when state affairs were discussed, one Diarist held the brush and recorded in front, and historiographers followed.
translations.idiomatic: After each court session, when state affairs were discussed, one Diarist took notes in front of the throne while historiographers followed along.

sentences.zh: 其後，復置起居舍人，分侍左右，秉筆隨宰相入殿；

translations.literal: Later Diarist-Recorders were restored, attending on left and right, brush in hand following the chief ministers into the hall;
translations.idiomatic: Later Diarist-Recorders were restored, attending on left and right with brush in hand, following the chief ministers into the hall;

sentences.zh: 若仗在紫宸內閤，則夾香案分立殿下，直第二螭首，和墨濡筆，皆即坳處，時號螭頭。

translations.literal: if the session was in the Zichen Inner Hall, they stood flanking the incense table below the steps, aligned with the second dragon-head bracket, grinding ink and wetting the brush—all at the recessed spot, then called 'dragon head.'
translations.idiomatic: if court was held in the Zichen Inner Hall, they stood flanking the incense table below the steps, aligned with the second dragon-head bracket, grinding ink and wetting their brushes at the recessed spot then called 'dragon head.'

sentences.zh: 高宗臨朝不決事，有司所奏，唯辭見而已。

translations.literal: When Gaozong held court he did not decide affairs; what the offices reported was only seen in written form.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong held court he did not decide affairs in person; what the offices reported reached him only in written form.

sentences.zh: 許敬宗、李義府為相，奏請多畏人之知也，命起居郎、舍人對仗承旨，仗下，與百官皆出，不復聞機務矣。

translations.literal: When Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu were chief ministers, many of their memorials and requests feared others' knowledge; they ordered Diarists and Diarist-Recorders to receive instructions facing the throne, and after court, together with all officials, departed—no longer hearing state secrets.
translations.idiomatic: When Xu Jingzong and Li Yifu served as chief ministers, many of their memorials and requests were matters they did not wish others to know; they ordered Diarists and Diarist-Recorders to receive instructions facing the throne, and after court all officials departed together—no longer hearing confidential state business.

sentences.zh: 長壽中，宰相姚璹建議：仗下後，宰相一人，錄軍國政要，為時政紀，月送史館。

translations.literal: During the Changshou era, Chief Minister Yao Shou proposed: after court, one chief minister should record the essentials of military and state affairs as a Current Affairs Chronicle, sent monthly to the Historiography Office.
translations.idiomatic: During the Changshou era (692–694), Chief Minister Yao Shou proposed that after court one chief minister should record the essentials of military and state affairs as a Current Affairs Chronicle, to be sent monthly to the Historiography Office.

sentences.zh: 然率推美讓善，事非其實，未幾亦罷。

translations.literal: Yet they generally extolled the good and yielded praise, so that matters were not true to fact, and before long this too was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the records generally extolled virtues and avoided faults, so that events were not true to fact, and before long this practice too was abolished.

sentences.zh: 而起居郎猶因制敕，稍稍筆削，以廣國史之闕。

translations.literal: Yet the Diarists still, following edicts and orders, gradually edited and trimmed to fill gaps in the national history.
translations.idiomatic: The Diarists nonetheless continued, following edicts and orders, gradually to edit and trim their records to fill gaps in the national history.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人本記言之職，唯編詔書，不及它事。

translations.literal: The Diarist-Recorder's office was originally for recording speech, but compiled only edicts and orders, not touching other matters.
translations.idiomatic: The Diarist-Recorder's office was originally charged with recording the emperor's words, but came to compile only edicts and orders, not touching other matters.

sentences.zh: 開元初，復詔脩史官非供奉者，皆隨仗而入，位於起居郎、舍人之次。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan an edict again ordered that historiographers not on special assignment all enter with the court session, taking places after the Diarists and Diarist-Recorders.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Kaiyuan era (713–741) an edict again ordered that historiographers not on special assignment all enter with the court session, taking places after the Diarists and Diarist-Recorders.

sentences.zh: 及李林甫專權，又廢。

translations.literal: When Li Linfu monopolized power, this was again abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Linfu monopolized power, this practice was again abolished.

sentences.zh: 大和九年，詔入閤日，起居郎、舍人具紙筆立螭頭下，復貞觀故事。

translations.literal: In Dahe 9 an edict ordered that on days when the emperor entered the inner hall, Diarists and Diarist-Recorders should prepare paper and brush and stand below the dragon head, restoring the Zhenguan precedent.
translations.idiomatic: In Dahe 9 (835) an edict ordered that on days when the emperor entered the inner hall, Diarists and Diarist-Recorders should prepare paper and brush and stand below the dragon-head bracket, restoring the Zhenguan precedent.

sentences.zh: 有令史三人，贊者六人。

translations.literal: There were three Clerks and six Announcers.
translations.idiomatic: The office had three Clerks and six Announcers.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年置起居郎，廢舍人。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 3 the Diarist was established and the Diarist-Recorder abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 (629) the office of Diarist was established and the Diarist-Recorder abolished.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年曰左史，天授元年亦如之。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 2 it was called Left Historian; in Tianshou 1 likewise.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 2 (662) the title became Left Historian; in Tianshou 1 (690) the same title was used.

sentences.zh: 典儀二人，從九品下。

translations.literal: Two Masters of Ceremonies, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Masters of Ceremonies, ranked at lower ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌贊唱及殿中版位之次，侍中版奏中嚴、外辦，亦贊焉。

translations.literal: They managed ceremonial announcements and the order of tablet positions in the hall; when the Vice Grand Councilor presented the tablet memorial for inner vigilance and outer preparation, they also announced.
translations.idiomatic: They managed ceremonial announcements and the order of tablet stations in the hall; when the Vice Grand Councilor presented the tablet memorial for the inner and outer vigils, they announced those rites as well.

sentences.zh: 隋謁者臺有典儀，武德五年復置，隸門下省。

translations.literal: The Sui Receptionist Office had Masters of Ceremonies; in Wude 5 they were reestablished, subordinate to the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui had Masters of Ceremonies in the Receptionist Office; in Wude 5 they were restored and placed under the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 城門郎四人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Four Gate Masters, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Gate Masters, ranked at upper sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌京城、皇城、宮殿諸門開闔之節，奉管鑰而出納之。

translations.literal: They managed the rules for opening and closing the gates of the capital, imperial city, and palace, receiving custody of keys and issuing them.
translations.idiomatic: They regulated the opening and closing of the capital, imperial city, and palace gates, taking custody of the keys and dispensing them as needed.

sentences.zh: 開則先外後內，闔則先內後外；

translations.literal: When opening, first outer then inner; when closing, first inner then outer;
translations.idiomatic: When opening the gates, the outer gates came first and the inner gates afterward; when closing them, the inner gates came first and the outer gates afterward;

sentences.zh: 啟閉有時，不以時則詣閤覆奏。

translations.literal: Opening and closing had fixed times; if not at the proper time, they went to the gate pavilion and reported back for confirmation.
translations.idiomatic: Opening and closing followed fixed hours; if a gate was opened or closed outside those hours, they went to the gate office and reported back for imperial confirmation.

sentences.zh: 有令史二人，書令史二人。

translations.literal: There were two Clerks and two Recording Clerks.
translations.idiomatic: The office had two Clerks and two Recording Clerks.

sentences.zh: 武德五年，置門僕八百人，番上送管鑰。

translations.literal: In Wude 5, eight hundred gate servants were established, rotating on duty to deliver keys.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 5 eight hundred gate servants were assigned, serving in rotation to deliver the keys.

sentences.zh: 符寶郎四人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Four Credential and Seal Masters, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Credential and Seal Masters, ranked at upper sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌天子八寶及國之符節。

translations.literal: They managed the Son of Heaven's eight imperial seals and the state's tallies and credentials.
translations.idiomatic: They kept the emperor's eight imperial seals and the state's tallies and credentials of authority.

sentences.zh: 有事則請於內，既事則奉而藏之。

translations.literal: When needed they requested them from the inner palace; once the matter was done they presented them back for storage.
translations.idiomatic: When they were needed for business, the masters requested them from the inner palace; once the business was finished, they returned them for safekeeping.

sentences.zh: 大朝會，則奉寶進于御座；

translations.literal: At great court assemblies, they presented the seals before the imperial throne;
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies they presented the imperial seals before the throne;

sentences.zh: 行幸，則奉以從焉。

translations.literal: When the emperor traveled, they carried them along.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor traveled, they carried the seals with him.

sentences.zh: 大事出符，則藏其左而班其右，以合中外之契，兼以敕書；

translations.literal: For major matters issuing tallies, they kept the left half and distributed the right half, to match inner and outer tokens, together with an authorization edict;
translations.idiomatic: When major business required issuing tallies, they kept the left half and distributed the right half so that inner and outer tokens could be matched, together with an authorization edict;

sentences.zh: 小事則降符函封，使合而行之。

translations.literal: For minor matters they issued sealed tally cases for the halves to be matched and carried out.
translations.idiomatic: for minor matters they issued sealed tally cases so that the halves could be matched and the order executed.

sentences.zh: 凡命將、遣使，皆請旌、節，旌以顓賞，節以顓殺。

translations.literal: Whenever generals were appointed or envoys dispatched, banners and credentials were requested; banners for exclusive reward authority, credentials for exclusive execution authority.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever generals were appointed or envoys dispatched, banners and credentials of authority were requested—the banner for exclusive power to reward, the credential for exclusive power to punish.

sentences.zh: 有令史二人，書令史三人，主寶二人，主符四人，主節四人。

translations.literal: There were two Clerks, three Recording Clerks, two Seal Custodians, four Tally Custodians, and four Credential Custodians.
translations.idiomatic: The office had two Clerks, three Recording Clerks, two Seal Custodians, four Tally Custodians, and four Credential Custodians.

sentences.zh: 武后延載元年，改符璽郎曰符寶郎；

translations.literal: In Yan Zai 1 under Empress Wu, Credential-Seal Masters were renamed Credential and Seal Masters;
translations.idiomatic: In Yan Zai 1 under Empress Wu, the Credential-Seal Masters were renamed Credential and Seal Masters;

sentences.zh: 開元元年，亦曰符寶郎。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 1, they were also called Credential and Seal Masters.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 1 the title was again Credential and Seal Master.

sentences.zh: 弘文館學士，掌詳正圖籍，教授生徒；

translations.literal: Hongwen Institute Academicians managed verification and correction of maps and records and instructed students;
translations.idiomatic: The Hongwen Institute Academicians verified and corrected maps and records and instructed students;

sentences.zh: 朝廷制度沿革、禮儀輕重，皆參議焉。

translations.literal: They also participated in deliberating on institutional changes and the weight of ritual propriety.
translations.idiomatic: they also took part in deliberating changes in court institutions and the relative weight of ritual observances.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，置修文館于門下省；

translations.literal: In Wude 4, the Xiūwén Institute was established in the Chancellery;
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4 the Xiūwén Institute was established within the Chancellery;

sentences.zh: 九年，改曰弘文館。

translations.literal: In year 9 it was renamed the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: in year 9 it was renamed the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，詔京官職事五品已上子嗜書者二十四人，隸館習書，出禁中書法以授之。

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 1, an edict ordered twenty-four sons of capital officials of fifth rank and above who loved books to attach to the institute to study calligraphy, and imperial calligraphy from the inner palace was brought out to teach them.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 an edict selected twenty-four sons of capital officials of fifth rank or higher who loved books, attached them to the institute to study calligraphy, and had imperial calligraphy from the inner palace brought out to instruct them.

sentences.zh: 其後又置講經博士。

translations.literal: Later a Lecturer in the Classics was also established.
translations.idiomatic: Later a Lecturer in the Classics was also added.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳中，置詳正學士，校理圖籍。

translations.literal: During the Yifeng era, Textual Verification Academicians were established to collate maps and records.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yifeng era Textual Verification Academicians were established to collate maps and records.

sentences.zh: 武德後，五品以上曰學士，六品已下曰直學士，又有文學直館，皆它官領之。

translations.literal: After Wude, those of fifth rank and above were called Academicians, sixth rank and below Direct Academicians; there were also Literary Associates of the Institute, all held concurrently by other officials.
translations.idiomatic: After Wude, officials of fifth rank and above were called Academicians and those of sixth rank and below Direct Academicians; there were also Literary Associates of the Institute, all of whom held the post concurrently with other offices.

sentences.zh: 武后垂拱後，以宰相兼領館務，號館主；

translations.literal: After Empress Wu's Chuigong era, chief ministers concurrently held institute duties, called Institute Directors;
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu's Chuigong era chief ministers concurrently directed the institute and were called Institute Directors;

sentences.zh: 給事中一人判館事。

translations.literal: One Drafting Attendant adjudicated institute affairs.
translations.idiomatic: one Drafting Attendant adjudicated the institute's affairs.

sentences.zh: 神龍元年，改弘文館曰昭文館，以避孝敬皇帝之名；

translations.literal: In Shenlong 1, the Hongwen Institute was renamed the Zhaowen Institute, to avoid the name of the Filial and Respectful Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: In Shenlong 1 the Hongwen Institute was renamed the Zhaowen Institute to avoid the name of the Filial and Respectful Emperor;

sentences.zh: 二年曰脩文館。

translations.literal: In year 2 it was called the Xiūwén Institute.
translations.idiomatic: in year 2 it was called the Xiūwén Institute.

sentences.zh: 景龍二年，置大學士四人，以象四時；

translations.literal: In Jinglong 2, four Grand Academicians were established, symbolizing the four seasons;
translations.idiomatic: In Jinglong 2 four Grand Academicians were established, symbolizing the four seasons;

sentences.zh: 學士八人，以象八節；

translations.literal: eight Academicians, symbolizing the eight seasonal divisions;
translations.idiomatic: eight Academicians, symbolizing the eight seasonal divisions;

sentences.zh: 直學士十二人，以象十二時。

translations.literal: twelve Direct Academicians, symbolizing the twelve double-hours.
translations.idiomatic: and twelve Direct Academicians, symbolizing the twelve double-hours.

sentences.zh: 景雲中，減其員數，復為昭文館。

translations.literal: During the Jingyun era, their numbers were reduced and it was again the Zhaowen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingyun era their numbers were reduced and the institute was again called the Zhaowen Institute.

sentences.zh: 開元七年曰弘文館，置校書郎，又有校理、讎校錯誤等官。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 7 it was called the Hongwen Institute; Text Collators were established, and there were also offices for collation, proofreading, and error correction.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 7 it was again called the Hongwen Institute; Text Collators were established, along with offices for collation, proofreading, and error correction.

sentences.zh: 長慶三年，與詳正學士、講經博士皆罷，顓以五品以上曰學士，六品以下曰直學士，未登朝為直館。

translations.literal: In Changqing 3, Textual Verification Academicians and the Lecturer in the Classics were all abolished; exclusively those of fifth rank and above were called Academicians, sixth rank and below Direct Academicians, and those not yet holding court office were Direct Associates.
translations.idiomatic: In Changqing 3 the Textual Verification Academicians and the Lecturer in the Classics were all abolished; thereafter only officials of fifth rank and above were called Academicians, those of sixth rank and below Direct Academicians, and those not yet holding court office Direct Associates.

sentences.zh: 校書郎二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two Text Collators, upper ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Text Collators, ranked at upper ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌校理典籍、刊正錯謬。

translations.literal: They managed collation of classics and correction of errors.
translations.idiomatic: They collated the classics and corrected textual errors.

sentences.zh: 凡學生教授、考試，如國子之制。

translations.literal: For instruction and examination of students, the regulations were like those of the Directorate of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Instruction and examination of students followed the regulations of the Directorate of Education.

sentences.zh: 有學生三十八人，令史二人，楷書十二人，供進筆二人，典書二人，搨書手三人，筆匠三人，熟紙裝潢匠八人，亭長二人，掌固四人。

translations.literal: There were thirty-eight students, two Clerks, twelve Regular Script copyists, two brush-supply attendants, two archive keepers, three rubbing copyists, three brush makers, eight paper-mounting craftsmen, two station chiefs, and four watchmen.
translations.idiomatic: The institute had thirty-eight students, two Clerks, twelve Regular Script copyists, two brush-supply attendants, two archive keepers, three rubbing copyists, three brush makers, eight paper-mounting craftsmen, two station chiefs, and four watchmen.

sentences.zh: 中書省中書令二人，正二品。

translations.literal: In the Secretariat, two Grand Secretaries, upper second rank.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat had two Grand Secretaries, ranked at upper second grade.

sentences.zh: 掌佐天子執大政，而總判省事。

translations.literal: They assisted the Son of Heaven in governing major affairs and held overall adjudication of departmental business.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted the emperor in governing major affairs and held overall authority to adjudicate Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 凡王言之制有七：一曰冊書，立皇后、皇太子，封諸王，臨軒冊命則用之；

translations.literal: There were seven forms of royal words: first, investiture documents, used when investing the empress, crown prince, or enfeoffing princes at the imperial steps;
translations.idiomatic: Imperial pronouncements took seven forms. The first was the investiture document, used when investing an empress or crown prince, enfeoffing princes, or conferring titles before the imperial steps;

sentences.zh: 二曰制書，大賞罰、赦宥慮囚、大除授則用之；

translations.literal: second, decree documents, used for major rewards and punishments, amnesties and review of prisoners, and major appointments and dismissals;
translations.idiomatic: second, the decree document, used for major rewards and punishments, amnesties and review of prisoners, and major appointments and dismissals;

sentences.zh: 三曰慰勞制書，褒勉贊勞則用之；

translations.literal: third, commendation decrees, used to praise, encourage, and commend merit;
translations.idiomatic: third, the commendation decree, used to praise, encourage, and commend merit;

sentences.zh: 四曰發敕，廢置州縣、增減官吏、發兵、除免官爵、授六品以上官則用之；

translations.literal: fourth, dispatch edicts, used to abolish or establish prefectures and counties, increase or reduce officials, mobilize troops, remove ranks and titles, and appoint officials of sixth rank and above;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, the dispatch edict, used to abolish or establish prefectures and counties, increase or reduce officials, mobilize troops, strip ranks and titles, and appoint officials of sixth rank or higher;

sentences.zh: 五曰敕旨，百官奏請施行則用之；

translations.literal: fifth, edict directives, used when the hundred offices memorialized requests for implementation;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, the edict directive, used when the hundred offices memorialized requests for implementation;

sentences.zh: 六曰論事敕書，戒約臣下則用之；

translations.literal: sixth, advisory edict letters, used to admonish and bind subordinates;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, the advisory edict letter, used to admonish and bind subordinates;

sentences.zh: 七曰敕牒，隨事承制，不易於舊則用之。

translations.literal: seventh, edict slips, used when following established precedent for matters that did not alter the old arrangements.
translations.idiomatic: and seventh, the edict slip, used for routine matters that followed established precedent without altering older arrangements.

sentences.zh: 皆宣署申覆，然後行焉。

translations.literal: All were promulgated, signed, and reported back before being executed.
translations.idiomatic: All were promulgated, signed, and reported back for confirmation before they could be executed.

sentences.zh: 大祭祀，則相禮；

translations.literal: At great sacrifices, they assisted with ritual;
translations.idiomatic: At great sacrifices they assisted with the rites;

sentences.zh: 親征纂嚴，則戒飭百官；

translations.literal: When the emperor personally campaigned and marshaled strictness, they admonished the hundred offices;
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor personally took the field and marshaled strict discipline, they admonished the hundred offices;

sentences.zh: 臨軒冊命，則讀冊；

translations.literal: At investiture before the imperial steps, they read the investiture document;
translations.idiomatic: at investiture before the imperial steps they read the investiture document;

sentences.zh: 若命於朝，則宣授而已；

translations.literal: If the appointment was made at court, they simply proclaimed and conferred it;
translations.idiomatic: if the appointment was made at court, they simply proclaimed and conferred it;

sentences.zh: 冊太子，則授璽綬。

translations.literal: When investing the crown prince, they presented the seal and cord.
translations.idiomatic: when investing the crown prince, they presented the seal and cord of office.

sentences.zh: 凡制詔文章獻納，以授記事之官。

translations.literal: All decree documents and memorial submissions were handed to the recording officials.
translations.idiomatic: All decree documents and submitted writings were handed to the recording officials.

sentences.zh: 武德三年，改內書省曰中書省，內書令曰中書令。

translations.literal: In Wude 3, the Inner Secretariat was renamed the Secretariat and the Inner Secretary the Grand Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 3 the Inner Secretariat was renamed the Secretariat and the Inner Secretary became the Grand Secretary.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，改中書省曰西臺，中書令曰右相。

translations.literal: In Longshuo 1, the Secretariat was renamed the Western Terrace and the Grand Secretary the Right Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In Longshuo 1 the Secretariat was renamed the Western Terrace and the Grand Secretary became the Right Minister.

sentences.zh: 光宅元年，改中書省曰鳳閣，中書令曰內史。

translations.literal: In Guangzhai 1, the Secretariat was renamed the Phoenix Pavilion and the Grand Secretary the Inner Historian.
translations.idiomatic: In Guangzhai 1 the Secretariat was renamed the Phoenix Pavilion and the Grand Secretary became the Inner Historian.

sentences.zh: 開元元年，改中書省曰紫微省，中書令曰紫微令。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 1, the Secretariat was renamed the Ziwei Department and the Grand Secretary the Ziwei Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 1 the Secretariat was renamed the Ziwei Department and the Grand Secretary became the Ziwei Director.

sentences.zh: 天寶元年曰右相，至大曆五年，紫微侍郎乃復為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In Tianbao 1 it was called Right Minister; by Dali 5 the Ziwei Vice Director was again called Secretariat Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianbao 1 the title became Right Minister; by Dali 5 the Ziwei Vice Director had again become the Secretariat Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 侍郎二人，正三品。

translations.literal: Two Vice Directors, upper third rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Vice Directors, ranked at upper third grade.

sentences.zh: 掌貳令之職，朝廷大政參議焉。

translations.literal: They assisted in the duties of the Director and participated in deliberating major court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: They assisted the Grand Secretary and took part in deliberating major court affairs.

sentences.zh: 臨軒冊命，為使，則持冊書授之。

translations.literal: At investiture before the imperial steps, when serving as envoy, they held the investiture document and conferred it.
translations.idiomatic: At investiture before the imperial steps, when serving as envoy, they held the investiture document and conferred it.

sentences.zh: 四夷來朝，則受其表疏而奏之；

translations.literal: When the four barbarians came to court, they received their petitions and memorialized them;
translations.idiomatic: When foreign envoys came to court, they received their petitions and memorialized them;

sentences.zh: 獻贄幣，則受以付有司。

translations.literal: When tribute gifts were presented, they received them and handed them to the appropriate offices.
translations.idiomatic: when tribute gifts were presented, they received them and handed them to the appropriate offices.

sentences.zh: 舍人六人，正五品上。

translations.literal: Six Secretariat Drafters, upper fifth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were six Secretariat Drafters, ranked at upper fifth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌侍進奏，參議表章。

translations.literal: They attended and presented memorials and participated in deliberating petitions.
translations.idiomatic: They attended court, presented memorials, and participated in deliberating petitions.

sentences.zh: 凡詔旨制敕、璽書冊命，皆起草進畫；

translations.literal: All edict directives, decrees, imperial seal documents, and investitures were drafted and submitted for approval;
translations.idiomatic: All edict directives, decrees, imperial seal documents, and investitures were drafted and submitted for imperial approval;

sentences.zh: 既下，則署行。

translations.literal: Once issued, they signed for execution.
translations.idiomatic: once issued, they signed them for execution.

sentences.zh: 其禁有四：一曰漏洩，二曰稽緩，三曰違失，四曰忘誤。

translations.literal: Four prohibitions applied: first, leakage; second, delay; third, violation and error; fourth, negligence and mistake.
translations.idiomatic: Four offenses were forbidden: leakage, delay, violation and error, and negligence and mistake.

sentences.zh: 制敕既行，有誤則奏改之。

translations.literal: Once decrees were issued, if there were errors they memorialized for correction.
translations.idiomatic: Once a decree had been issued, any error was corrected by memorial.

sentences.zh: 大朝會，諸方起居，則受其表狀；

translations.literal: At great court assemblies, for regional routine reports they received the petition forms;
translations.idiomatic: At great court assemblies they received routine reports from the regions;

sentences.zh: 大捷、祥瑞，百寮表賀亦如之。

translations.literal: For great victories and auspicious omens, congratulatory petitions from the hundred offices were handled likewise.
translations.idiomatic: for great victories and auspicious omens they likewise received congratulatory petitions from the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 冊命大臣，則使持節讀冊命；

translations.literal: When investing high ministers, as envoy they held credentials and read the investiture;
translations.idiomatic: when investing high ministers they served as envoy, holding credentials and reading the investiture;

sentences.zh: 將帥有功及大賓客，則勞問。

translations.literal: For meritorious generals and important guests, they conveyed imperial condolences and inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: for meritorious generals and important guests they conveyed the emperor's condolences and inquiries.

sentences.zh: 與給事中及御史三司鞫冤滯。

translations.literal: Together with Drafting Attendants and the censorate's three offices they investigated grievances and delays in justice.
translations.idiomatic: Together with the Drafting Attendants and the censorate's three offices they investigated grievances and delays in justice.

sentences.zh: 百司奏議考課，皆預裁焉。

translations.literal: For memorials, deliberations, and performance reviews from the hundred offices, they all participated in adjudication.
translations.idiomatic: They also took part in adjudicating memorials, deliberations, and performance reviews from the hundred offices.

sentences.zh: 以久次者一人為閣老，判本省雜事；

translations.literal: The one senior in tenure became Elder of the Pavilion, adjudicating miscellaneous affairs of the department;
translations.idiomatic: The drafter longest in tenure became Elder of the Pavilion and adjudicated miscellaneous Secretariat affairs;

sentences.zh: 又一人知制誥，顓進畫，給食于政事堂；

translations.literal: another one managed imperial writings, exclusively submitting drafts, and was fed at the Hall of Governance;
translations.idiomatic: another managed imperial writings, exclusively submitting drafts, and was fed at the Hall of Governance;

sentences.zh: 其餘分署制敕。

translations.literal: The rest divided signing of decrees.
translations.idiomatic: the rest divided responsibility for signing decrees.

sentences.zh: 以六員分押尚書六曹，佐宰相判案，同署乃奏，唯樞密遷授不預。

translations.literal: The six members divided supervision of the six bureaus of the Ministry of Civil Affairs, assisting the chief minister in adjudicating cases; only when all signed together was it memorialized—except for confidential personnel appointments.
translations.idiomatic: The six drafters divided supervision of the Ministry of Civil Affairs' six bureaus, assisting the chief minister in adjudicating cases; a matter was memorialized only after all had signed—except for confidential personnel appointments.

sentences.zh: 姚崇為紫微令，奏：大事，舍人為商量狀，與本狀皆下紫微令，判二狀之是否，然後乃奏。

translations.literal: When Yao Chong was Ziwei Director, he memorialized: on major matters, the Secretariat Drafter prepared a deliberation summary together with the original memorial, both sent to the Ziwei Director who judged whether the two documents accorded, and only then was it memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: When Yao Chong was Ziwei Director, he memorialized that on major matters the Secretariat Drafter should prepare a deliberation summary to accompany the original memorial; both documents went to the Ziwei Director, who judged whether they accorded, and only then was the matter memorialized.

sentences.zh: 開元初，以它官掌詔敕策命，謂之「兼知制誥」。

translations.literal: Early in Kaiyuan, when other officials managed edicts, decrees, and appointments, they were called "Concurrently Managing Imperial Writings."
translations.idiomatic: Early in Kaiyuan, when other officials managed edicts, decrees, and appointments, they were called "Concurrently Managing Imperial Writings."

sentences.zh: 肅宗即位，又以它官知中書舍人事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Suzong ascended, other officials again managed the duties of Secretariat Drafters.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Suzong ascended the throne, other officials again managed the duties of Secretariat Drafters.

sentences.zh: 兵興，急於權便，政去臺閣，決遣顓出宰相，自是舍人不復押六曹之奏。

translations.literal: With war underway, urgency favored expedience; governance departed from the pavilion offices, and decisions issued exclusively from the chief minister—from then on Secretariat Drafters no longer supervised memorials from the six bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: With war underway, urgency favored expedience; governance departed from the pavilion offices, and decisions issued exclusively from the chief minister—from then on Secretariat Drafters no longer supervised memorials from the six bureaus.

sentences.zh: 會昌末，宰相李德裕建議：臺閣常務、州縣奏請，復以舍人平處可否。

translations.literal: Late in Huichang, Chief Minister Li Deyu proposed: for routine pavilion business and county and prefecture petitions, Secretariat Drafters should again adjudicate what was feasible.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Huichang Chief Minister Li Deyu proposed that for routine pavilion business and petitions from prefectures and counties, Secretariat Drafters should again adjudicate what was feasible.

sentences.zh: 先是，知制誥率用前行正郎，宣宗時，選尚書郎為之。

translations.literal: Previously, those managing imperial writings were generally drawn from former Department of State Affairs regular directors of upper rank; under Emperor Xuanzong, Ministry of Civil Affairs directors were selected.
translations.idiomatic: Previously those who managed imperial writings were generally drawn from former Department of State Affairs regular directors of upper rank; under Emperor Xuanzong Ministry of Civil Affairs directors were selected instead.

sentences.zh: 主書四人，從七品上。

translations.literal: Four Recording Masters, upper seventh rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Recording Masters, ranked at upper seventh grade.

sentences.zh: 主事四人，從八品下。

translations.literal: Four Section Chiefs, lower eighth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Section Chiefs, ranked at lower eighth grade.

sentences.zh: 有令史二十五人，書令史五十人，能書四人，蕃書譯語十人，乘驛二十人，傳制十人，亭長十八人，掌固二十四人，裝制敕匠一人，脩補制敕匠五十人，掌函、掌案各二十人。

translations.literal: There were twenty-five Clerks, fifty Recording Clerks, four skilled scribes, ten foreign-script translators, twenty post-riders, ten decree couriers, eighteen station chiefs, twenty-four watchmen, one decree-binding craftsman, fifty decree-repair craftsmen, and twenty box keepers and twenty document keepers each.
translations.idiomatic: The office had twenty-five Clerks, fifty Recording Clerks, four skilled scribes, ten foreign-script translators, twenty post-riders, ten decree couriers, eighteen station chiefs, twenty-four watchmen, one decree-binding craftsman, fifty decree-repair craftsmen, and twenty box keepers and twenty document keepers each.

sentences.zh: 右散騎常侍二人，右諫議大夫四人，右補闕六人，右拾遺六人，掌如門下省。

translations.literal: Two Right Masters of Regular Attendance, four Right Remonstrance Masters, six Right Supplementers, and six Right Pickers-up—duties as in the Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Right Masters of Regular Attendance, four Right Remonstrance Masters, six Right Supplementers, and six Right Pickers-up, with duties the same as those in the Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 起居舍人二人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Two Diarist-Recorders, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Diarist-Recorders, ranked at upper sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌脩記言之史，錄制誥德音，如記事之制，季終以授國史。

translations.literal: They maintained the history of recorded speech, recorded decree benevolences, following the recording regulations; at quarter's end they handed them to the National Historiographer.
translations.idiomatic: They maintained the history of recorded speech and recorded benevolent edicts, following the recording regulations; at the end of each quarter they handed the records to the National Historiographer.

sentences.zh: 有楷書手四人，典二人。

translations.literal: There were four Regular Script copyists and two archivists.
translations.idiomatic: The office had four Regular Script copyists and two archivists.

sentences.zh: 通事舍人十六人，從六品上。

translations.literal: Sixteen Reception Masters, upper sixth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were sixteen Reception Masters, ranked at upper sixth grade.

sentences.zh: 掌朝見引納、殿庭通奏。

translations.literal: They managed introduction at audiences and transmission of memorials in the court hall.
translations.idiomatic: They managed introductions at audiences and the transmission of memorials in the court hall.

sentences.zh: 凡近臣入侍、文武就列，則導其進退，而贊其拜起、出入之節。

translations.literal: Whenever close attendants entered to serve or civil and military officials took their places, they guided their advance and withdrawal and announced the protocol for bowing, rising, and entering and leaving.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever close attendants entered to serve or civil and military officials took their places, they guided their advance and withdrawal and announced the protocol for bowing, rising, entering, and leaving.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷納貢，皆受而進之。

translations.literal: When barbarians presented tribute, they all received it and presented it onward.
translations.idiomatic: When foreign peoples presented tribute, they received it and presented it onward.

sentences.zh: 軍出，則受命勞遣；

translations.literal: When armies went out, they received orders to convey greetings and send them off;
translations.idiomatic: When armies marched out, they received orders to convey the emperor's greetings and send the troops off;

sentences.zh: 既行，則每月存問將士之家，視其疾苦；

translations.literal: Once they departed, each month they inquired after the families of soldiers and officers, observing their hardships;
translations.idiomatic: once the armies had departed, they inquired each month after the families of soldiers and officers and looked into their hardships;

sentences.zh: 凱還，則郊迓。

translations.literal: When they returned in victory, they went to the outskirts to welcome them.
translations.idiomatic: when the armies returned in victory, they went to the outskirts to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 有令史十人，典謁十人，亭長十八人，掌固二十四人。

translations.literal: There were ten Clerks, ten reception attendants, eighteen station chiefs, and twenty-four watchmen.
translations.idiomatic: The office had ten Clerks, ten reception attendants, eighteen station chiefs, and twenty-four watchmen.

sentences.zh: 武德四年，廢謁者臺，改通事謁者曰通事舍人。

translations.literal: In Wude 4, the Receptionist Office was abolished and Palace Reception Attendants were renamed Reception Masters.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 4 the Receptionist Office was abolished and Palace Reception Attendants were renamed Reception Masters.

sentences.zh: 集賢殿書院學士、直學士、侍讀學士、脩撰官，掌刊緝經籍。

translations.literal: Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy Academicians, Direct Academicians, Reading Academicians, and Compilation Officials managed editing and collation of classics.
translations.idiomatic: The Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy Academicians, Direct Academicians, Reading Academicians, and Compilation Officials edited and collated the classics.

sentences.zh: 凡圖書遺逸、賢才隱滯，則承旨以求之。

translations.literal: For lost books and records, and for talented men held back in obscurity, they received orders to seek them out.
translations.idiomatic: When books or records were lost, or talented men languished in obscurity, they received imperial orders to seek them out.

sentences.zh: 謀慮可施於時，著述可行於世者，考其學術以聞。

translations.literal: For plans that could be applied in the present age and writings that could circulate in the world, they examined their learning and reported it.
translations.idiomatic: When plans could be applied to the times or writings could circulate in the world, they examined the author's learning and reported it upward.

sentences.zh: 凡承旨撰集文章、校理經籍，月終則進課於內，歲終則考最於外。

translations.literal: For all commissioned compilation of writings and collation of classics, at month's end they submitted progress reports to the inner palace, and at year's end performance was evaluated externally.
translations.idiomatic: For all commissioned writing and collation of the classics, they submitted monthly progress reports to the inner palace and underwent annual performance review outside it.

sentences.zh: 開元五年，乾元殿寫四部書，置乾元院使，有刊正官四人，以一人判事；

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 5, the four categories of books were copied at the Qianyuan Hall; a Qianyuan Academy commissioner was established, with four Text Correctors, one of whom adjudicated affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 5 the four categories of books were copied at the Qianyuan Hall; a Qianyuan Academy commissioner was appointed, with four Text Correctors, one of whom adjudicated affairs;

sentences.zh: 押院中使一人，掌出入宣奏，領中官監守院門；

translations.literal: one eunuch commissioner to supervise the academy, managing entry and exit announcements and leading palace eunuchs to guard the academy gate;
translations.idiomatic: one eunuch commissioner supervised the academy, managing entry and exit announcements and directing palace eunuchs to guard the academy gate;

sentences.zh: 知書官八人，分掌四庫書。

translations.literal: eight Book Managers, each managing one of the four storehouses of books.
translations.idiomatic: eight Book Managers, each responsible for one of the four book storehouses.

sentences.zh: 六年，乾元院更號麗正脩書院，置使及檢校官，改脩書官為麗正殿直學士。

translations.literal: In year 6, the Qianyuan Academy was renamed the Lizheng Book-Compilation Academy; a commissioner and inspection officials were established, and book compilers were renamed Lizheng Hall Direct Academicians.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 the Qianyuan Academy was renamed the Lizheng Book-Compilation Academy; a commissioner and inspection officials were appointed, and book compilers became Lizheng Hall Direct Academicians.

sentences.zh: 八年，加文學直，又加脩撰、校理、刊正、校勘官。

translations.literal: In year 8, Literary Associates were added, along with Compilation, Collation, Text Correction, and Proofreading officials.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8 Literary Associates were added, along with officials for compilation, collation, text correction, and proofreading.

sentences.zh: 十一年，置麗正院脩書學士；

translations.literal: In year 11, Lizheng Academy Book-Compilation Academicians were established;
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 Lizheng Academy Book-Compilation Academicians were established;

sentences.zh: 光順門外，亦置書院。

translations.literal: Outside the Guangshun Gate, an academy was also established.
translations.idiomatic: an academy was also established outside the Guangshun Gate.

sentences.zh: 十二年，東都明福門外亦置麗正書院。

translations.literal: In year 12, the Lizheng Academy was also established outside the Mingfu Gate in the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 the Lizheng Academy was also established outside the Mingfu Gate in the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改麗正脩書院為集賢殿書院，五品以上為學士，六品以下為直學士，宰相一人為學士知院事，常侍一人為副知院事，又置判院一人、押院中使一人。

translations.literal: In year 13, the Lizheng Book-Compilation Academy was renamed the Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy; those of fifth rank and above were Academicians, sixth rank and below Direct Academicians; one chief minister served as Academician managing academy affairs, one Regular Attendant as deputy manager; one academy adjudicator and one eunuch academy supervisor were also established.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13 the Lizheng Book-Compilation Academy was renamed the Hall of Assembled Worthies Academy; officials of fifth rank and above became Academicians and those of sixth rank and below Direct Academicians; one chief minister served as Academician managing academy affairs, one Regular Attendant as deputy manager, and one academy adjudicator and one eunuch academy supervisor were also appointed.

sentences.zh: 玄宗嘗選耆儒，日一人侍讀，以質史籍疑義，至是，置集賢院侍講學士、侍讀直學士。

translations.literal: Emperor Xuanzong had once selected aged scholars, one per day to attend readings, to question them on doubtful points in historical records; at this time, Hall of Assembled Worthies Lecture Academicians and Reading Direct Academicians were established.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong had once selected aged scholars, one each day to attend readings and question them on doubtful points in historical records; at this time Hall of Assembled Worthies Lecture Academicians and Reading Direct Academicians were established.

sentences.zh: 其後，又增脩撰官、校理官、待制官、留院官、知檢討官、文學直之員；

translations.literal: Afterward the numbers of Compilation Officials, Collation Officials, Drafting Attendants, Academy Retention Officials, Inspection Supervisors, and Literary Associates were increased;
translations.idiomatic: Afterward the numbers of Compilation Officials, Collation Officials, Drafting Attendants, Academy Retention Officials, Inspection Supervisors, and Literary Associates were increased;

sentences.zh: 募能書者為書直及寫御書人，其後亦以前資、常選、三衞、散官五品以上子孫為之；

translations.literal: Able scribes were recruited as Book Associates and Imperial Book Copyists; later sons of former officials, regular appointees, Three Guards, and unofficial officials of fifth rank and above were also selected;
translations.idiomatic: Able scribes were recruited as Book Associates and Imperial Book Copyists; later sons of former officials, regular appointees, Three Guards members, and unofficial officials of fifth rank and above were also selected;

sentences.zh: 又置畫直。

translations.literal: Painting Associates were also established.
translations.idiomatic: Painting Associates were also added.

sentences.zh: 至十九年，以書直、畫直、搨書有官者為直院。

translations.literal: By year 19, Book Associates, Painting Associates, and rub-copy scribes who held official posts were made the Direct Academy.
translations.idiomatic: By year 19 Book Associates, Painting Associates, and rub-copy scribes who held official posts were organized as the Direct Academy.

sentences.zh: 至德二年，置大學士。

translations.literal: In Zhide 2, Grand Academicians were established.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhide 2 Grand Academicians were established.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，置編錄官；

translations.literal: Early in the Zhenyuan era, Compilation and Recording Officials were established;
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhenyuan era Compilation and Recording Officials were established;

sentences.zh: 四年，罷大學士；

translations.literal: in year 4, Grand Academicians were abolished;
translations.idiomatic: in year 4 the Grand Academicians were abolished;

sentences.zh: 八年，罷校理，置校書四人、正字二人。

translations.literal: in year 8, Collation Officials were abolished, and four Text Collators and two Proofreaders were established.
translations.idiomatic: in year 8 Collation Officials were abolished and four Text Collators and two Proofreaders were appointed.

sentences.zh: 元和二年，復置集賢校理，罷校書、正字；

translations.literal: In Yuanhe 2, Hall of Assembled Worthies Collation Officials were restored and Text Collators and Proofreaders abolished;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 2 Hall of Assembled Worthies Collation Officials were restored and Text Collators and Proofreaders were abolished;

sentences.zh: 四年，集賢御書院學士、直學士皆用五品，如開元故事，以學士一人年高者判院事，非登朝官者為校理，餘皆罷。

translations.literal: In year 4, Hall of Assembled Worthies Imperial Book Academy Academicians and Direct Academicians all used fifth rank, following the Kaiyuan precedent; the senior Academician adjudicated academy affairs, those not holding court office became Collation Officials, and the rest were abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4 Hall of Assembled Worthies Imperial Book Academy Academicians and Direct Academicians all held fifth rank, following the Kaiyuan precedent; the senior Academician adjudicated academy affairs, those not holding court office became Collation Officials, and all other posts were abolished.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗即位，命京官五品以上，更宿中書、門下兩省，以備訪問。

translations.literal: Initially, when Emperor Taizong ascended, he ordered capital officials of fifth rank and above to lodge in rotation at the Secretariat and Chancellery, ready for consultation.
translations.idiomatic: Initially, when Emperor Taizong ascended the throne, he ordered capital officials of fifth rank and above to lodge in rotation at the Secretariat and Chancellery, ready for imperial consultation.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，命弘文館學士一人，日待制于武德殿西門。

translations.literal: During the Yonghui era, one Hongwen Institute Academician was ordered to serve on draft daily at the west gate of the Wude Hall.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yonghui era one Hongwen Institute Academician was ordered to serve on draft daily at the west gate of the Wude Hall.

sentences.zh: 文明元年，詔京官五品以上清官，日一人待制于章善、明福門。

translations.literal: In Wenming 1, an edict ordered one pure official among capital officials of fifth rank and above to serve on draft daily at the Zhangshan and Mingfu gates.
translations.idiomatic: In Wenming 1 an edict ordered one pure official among capital officials of fifth rank and above to serve on draft daily at the Zhangshan and Mingfu gates.

sentences.zh: 先天末，又命朝集使六品以上二人，隨仗待制。

translations.literal: At the end of the Xiantian era, two Assembly Envoys of sixth rank and above were also ordered to serve on draft with the court session.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of the Xiantian era two Assembly Envoys of sixth rank and above were also ordered to serve on draft with the court session.

sentences.zh: 永泰時，勳臣罷節制，無職事，皆待制于集賢門，凡十三人。

translations.literal: During the Yongtai era, meritorious officials who had lost their military commands and had no duties all served on draft at the Hall of Assembled Worthies gate—thirteen in all.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongtai era meritorious officials who had lost their military commands and held no other duties all served on draft at the Hall of Assembled Worthies gate—thirteen in all.

sentences.zh: 崔祐甫為相，建議文官一品以上更直待制。

translations.literal: When Cui Youfu became chief minister, he proposed that civil officials of first rank and above serve on draft in rotation.
translations.idiomatic: When Cui Youfu became chief minister, he proposed that civil officials of first rank and above serve on draft in rotation.

sentences.zh: 其後著令，正衙待制官日二人。

translations.literal: Later this was written into regulation: two Drafting Attendants daily at the main court.
translations.idiomatic: Later this was written into regulation: two Drafting Attendants served daily at the main court.

sentences.zh: 校書四人，正九品下。

translations.literal: Four Text Collators, lower ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Text Collators, ranked at lower ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 正字二人，從九品上。

translations.literal: Two Proofreaders, upper sub-ninth rank.
translations.idiomatic: There were two Proofreaders, ranked at upper sub-ninth grade.

sentences.zh: 有中使一人，孔目官一人，專知御書檢討八人，知書官八人，書直、寫御書手九十人，畫直六人，裝書直十四人，造筆直四人，搨書六人，典四人。

translations.literal: There was one eunuch commissioner, one inventory clerk, eight specialists in imperial book inspection, eight Book Managers, ninety Book Associates and Imperial Book Copyists, six Painting Associates, fourteen book-binding associates, four brush makers, six rub-copy scribes, and four archivists.
translations.idiomatic: The academy had one eunuch commissioner, one inventory clerk, eight specialists in imperial book inspection, eight Book Managers, ninety Book Associates and Imperial Book Copyists, six Painting Associates, fourteen book-binding associates, four brush makers, six rub-copy scribes, and four archivists.

sentences.zh: 史館脩撰四人，掌脩國史。

translations.literal: Four Historiography Office Compilers, managing compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: There were four Historiography Office Compilers, who compiled the national history.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，置史館於門下省，以他官兼領，或卑位有才者亦以直館稱，以宰相涖脩撰；

translations.literal: In Zhenguan 3, the Historiography Office was established in the Chancellery; other officials held the post concurrently, and talented men of lower rank were also called Direct Associates; chief ministers supervised compilation;
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 3 the Historiography Office was established in the Chancellery; other officials held the post concurrently, and talented men of lower rank were also called Direct Associates; chief ministers supervised compilation;

sentences.zh: 又於中書省置祕書內省，脩五代史。

translations.literal: An Inner Secretariat Office was also established in the Secretariat to compile the history of the Five Dynasties.
translations.idiomatic: an Inner Secretariat Office was also established within the Secretariat to compile the history of the Five Dynasties.

sentences.zh: 開元二十年，李林甫以宰相監脩國史，建議以為中書切密之地，史官記事隸門下省，疏遠。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan 20, Li Linfu as chief minister supervised compilation of the national history and proposed that the Secretariat was the place of utmost confidentiality, while historiographers under the Chancellery were remote and distant.
translations.idiomatic: In Kaiyuan 20 Li Linfu, serving as chief minister supervising compilation of the national history, proposed that the Secretariat was the place of utmost confidentiality, while historiographers attached to the Chancellery were too remote.

sentences.zh: 於是諫議大夫、史館脩撰尹愔奏徙于中書省。

translations.literal: Thereupon Remonstrance Master and Historiography Office Compiler Yin Yin memorialized to move it to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Remonstrance Master and Historiography Office Compiler Yin Yin memorialized to move the office to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 天寶後，他官兼史職者曰史館脩撰，初入為直館。

translations.literal: After Tianbao, other officials who concurrently held historiography duties were called Historiography Office Compilers; newcomers began as Direct Associates.
translations.idiomatic: After Tianbao other officials who concurrently held historiography duties were called Historiography Office Compilers; newcomers began as Direct Associates.

sentences.zh: 元和六年，宰相裴垍建議：登朝官領史職者為脩撰，以官高一人判館事；

translations.literal: In Yuanhe 6, Chief Minister Pei Ji proposed: court officials who held historiography duties were Compilers, with the highest-ranked one adjudicating office affairs;
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanhe 6 Chief Minister Pei Ji proposed that court officials who held historiography duties should be Compilers, with the highest-ranked one adjudicating office affairs;

sentences.zh: 未登朝官皆為直館。
